comparison: Perfect agreement on POT1a/POT1b findings in mouse ESCs (C18-C20, C52-C53). Both evaluations find the evidence strongly supported. Peer reviewers explicitly highlight the POT1b dispensability as a novel, important insight, while OpenEval emphasizes the rigorous CRISPR-engineered experimental design.

Both address VTR frequency findings (C25, C45), but with different conclusions. OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED while acknowledging biological significance requires further investigation. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN and explicitly request additional experiments to determine if VTRs are increased at ssDNA regions, indicating incomplete findings.

Both address the mechanistic origin of ssDNA (C42-C43, C54-C55). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting the claims are appropriately speculative and lack direct determination of ssDNA sources. Peer reviewers also rate as UNCERTAIN and explicitly request speculation about whether ssDNA is a BIR intermediate and ask about ECTR contributions, confirming the mechanistic uncertainty.

Strong agreement on S1-END-seq findings showing ssDNA in ALT cells (C26-C28, C40, C57-C58). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes the clear quantitative distinction between ALT and non-ALT cells, while peer reviewers confirm the successful application of S1-END-seq to detect telomeric ssDNA. OpenEval suggests clinical validation would strengthen diagnostic utility claims.

Strong agreement on BLM-dependent ssDNA formation and link to ALT activity (C31-C33, C46, C48). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval highlights the TRF1-FokI rescue experiment as strong evidence for DSB-induced ssDNA formation. Peer reviewers explicitly confirm the demonstration that ssDNA is intrinsic to ALT and BLM-dependent.

Both address END-seq methodology validation (C34-C35, C59-C63). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes consistency across multiple cell lines and biological replicates. Peer reviewers explicitly affirm successful application with 'unprecedented depth and precision' and note the work 'clearly demonstrates' END-seq utility for telomere studies.

Both address T7 exonuclease validation experiments (C16, C51). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes the KL divergence analysis showing extreme divergence and notes the experimental design appropriately tests true terminal sequence detection. Peer reviewers accept these validation experiments without critique as supporting evidence.

Both address canonical terminal sequences in ALT cells (C21-C22, C2, C36-C37). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes consistency across 11 biological replicates in three ALT cell lines. Peer reviewers explicitly confirm the demonstration that the same ATC terminal sequence principle holds in ALT cells as in telomerase-positive cells.

Both address quantitative estimates of ssDNA regions (C30, C44, C49). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to different estimates (3 vs 5 regions) based on mathematical modeling requiring validation. Peer reviewers rate as SUPPORTED and explicitly accept the estimate of 'at least five regions of ssDNA' without challenge.

Both address POT1 depletion effects (C17, C3, C39 in OpenEval; C23-C24, C3, C39 in peer review). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasizes KL divergence analysis and multiple shRNA constructs. Peer reviewers confirm POT1-dependent canonical sequence maintenance in ALT cells without concerns.

Partial overlap on independence of 5' end regulation from elongation mechanism (C4, C38). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval addresses POT1 depletion effects and DDR response (C23-C24) alongside the independence claim. Peer reviewers implicitly support the independence conclusion through acceptance that ALT and non-ALT cells have the same terminal sequences.

Partial overlap on canonical terminal sequences in telomerase-positive cells (C12-C15). Both rate as SUPPORTED. OpenEval groups these with broader methodological validation claims. Peer reviewers specifically confirm verification of prior data showing ATC 5' terminal sequences in HeLa and RPE cells.

Minimal overlap on ALT cell classification (C41). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED but suggests testing on larger cell line panels. Peer reviewers include this claim within broader S1-END-seq findings rated as SUPPORTED, confirming the method can distinguish ALT from non-ALT cells.

OpenEval evaluates background/contextual claims (C1, C5-C11, C37, C56) as SUPPORTED, noting these represent well-established knowledge appropriately cited. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as reviewers focused on novel experimental findings rather than background claims.
